This Appeal, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice H.T. Narendra Prasad
 Oral Judgment
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the claimant challenging by the judgment dated 05.02.2018 passed by Mact,
Udupi (sitting at Kundapura) in Mvc No.721/2016.
2.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 28.06.2015 when the claimant along NC: 2024:KHC:37141 with others were traveling in car bearing registration No.KA-20-N-7255 from Haladi to Kundapura, at that time, the driver of the bus bearing No.KA-20-A-7723 drove the same at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, and over took the car and applied sudden break in order to avoid collusion against the motorcycle and hence the backside of the bus hit the car.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.

sentences.text: Upon service of notice, the respondent Nos.1, 2 and 4 appeared through counsel and only respondent No.2 filed written statements denying the averments made in NC: 2024:KHC:37141 the claim petition.
The respondent No.3, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petition and held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.10,220/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the respondent Nos.2 and 4 (both the Insurance Companies) to deposit the compensation amount equally along with interest at 50% each.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.
6. The learned counsel for the claimant has submitted that the claimant has sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
He has produced medical bills amounting to Rs.4,223/-.
Even after discharge from the hospital, he was not in a position to discharge his regular work.

He has NC:
2024:KHC:37141 suffered lot of pain during treatment.
Considering the same, the overall compensation granted by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Hence, he sought to allow the appeal.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the claimant has sustained simple injuries and he has not examined the doctor regarding nature of injuries and disability suffered by him.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and medical records, the Tribunal has granted just and reasonable compensation and it does not call for interference.
Hence, he sought to dismissal the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
9.
It is not in dispute that the claimant has sustained injuries in the accident occurred on 28.06.2015 due to negligence of drivers of the both the vehicles i.e., bus and car.
As per wound certificate, the claimant has sustained dento alveolar fracture of Mandible with subluxation of Haematoma over scalp.
He has produced medical bills amounting to Rs.4,223/-.
He has not examined the doctor regarding nature of injuries and disability suffered by him.

Therefore,
considering the evidence of the claimant, nature of injuries mentioned in the wound certificate and medical records, I am inclined to award a compensation of Rs.50,000/- as against Rs.10,220/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
11. In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
